analysis.investment_thesis: Emmvee has legitimate business quality — 28% ROCE and explosive revenue growth — but the Magic Formula breaks down here because the stock is priced for perfection with a trailing earnings yield of only 3.6% (EBIT 722 Cr / EV ~20,231 Cr), well below the 6% minimum threshold. You're paying a rich price for a capital-hungry solar manufacturer drowning in capex, which is precisely the profile the Magic Formula is designed to avoid.
key_strengths: ROCE of 28% (given) clears the Magic Formula's 25% excellence threshold, indicating genuine business quality
Revenue CAGR of 33.3% and operating income explosion from 120 Cr (2024) to 722 Cr (2025) show real operating leverage
OCF positive all 5 years with 614 Cr in 2025, confirming earnings are not purely accounting fiction
key_risks: Earnings yield only 3.6% (EBIT 722 Cr / EV 20,231 Cr) — far below the 6% floor; the stock is NOT cheap
FCF deeply negative three years running (-173, -440, -375 Cr) due to capex of 988 Cr in 2025 — high capital intensity destroys FCF conversion
Debt tripled in two years (524 Cr → 2,065 Cr); D/E of 2.15 on a capital-intensive solar business is leverage risk in a rising-rate or policy-reversal scenario
red_flags: Trailing earnings yield 3.6% — Magic Formula demands >12% for a buy; this fails the cheapness test decisively
ROE of 105% is misleading — driven by an artificially low equity base (140 Cr equity in 2023), not sustainable capital efficiency
Solar manufacturing is heavily policy-dependent (PLI, import tariffs); ROIC spike in 2025 may not be durable
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EV = Market Cap 18,385 + Total Debt 2,065 – Cash 219 = ~20,231 Cr. EBIT (Operating Income 2025) = 722 Cr. Earnings Yield = 722/20,231 = **3.6%** — this is less than one-third of the 12% target and below even the 6% minimum. On ROIC, the company reports ROCE of 28%, which is excellent by Magic Formula standards. But the Magic Formula requires BOTH metrics to score well. When earnings yield is this low, no amount of ROIC quality justifies a buy — you're simply overpaying for the quality.

The deeper concern is capital intensity. Capex ran 988 Cr in 2025 against OCF of 614 Cr, producing FCF of -375 Cr. Solar cell and module manufacturing requires relentless reinvestment, which is why Magic Formula typically produces poor results in this sector — high apparent ROIC gets eaten by capex in subsequent periods. Debt has ballooned from 524 Cr to 2,065 Cr in two years to fund this expansion. The forward P/E of 15.78 implies the market is pricing in a near-tripling of earnings — if that materialises, the story improves, but Greenblatt's formula is ruthlessly trailing-based for good reason: forward estimates are where investors get burned.
